name: Alpha-heavy chain disease

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic criteria for Alpha-heavy chain disease

criteria.description: Presence of abnormal alpha-heavy chain immunoglobulin deposits in small intestinal biopsy
Detection of monoclonal alpha-heavy chain protein in serum or intestinal secretions
Chronic malabsorption symptoms with weight loss and diarrhea
Immunohistochemical confirmation of alpha-heavy chain expression in lymphoid infiltrates

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation of alpha-heavy chain deposits plus detection of monoclonal alpha-heavy chain protein in serum or intestinal secretions
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires integration of clinical, histological, and immunological findings.

laboratory: Monoclonal alpha-heavy chain protein detected by serum protein electrophoresis or immunofixation
Anemia with iron deficiency or malabsorption pattern
imaging: CT scan showing thickening of small intestinal walls and mesenteric lymphadenopathy
Barium studies revealing mucosal irregularities and malabsorption features
genetic: No specific genetic mutations identified; disease is acquired
other: Histopathology demonstrating lymphoplasmacytic infiltration and alpha-heavy chain deposits in intestinal mucosa

distinguishingFeatures: Overlap with alpha-heavy chain disease but may include other heavy chain types
Absence of monoclonal alpha-heavy chain protein
Different histopathological features without lymphoplasmacytic infiltration
Neoplastic lymphoid proliferation without alpha-heavy chain deposits

redFlags: Rapid weight loss with severe malabsorption
Presence of monoclonal alpha-heavy chain protein in serum
references: Swerdlow SH, Campo E, Harris NL, et al. WHO Classification of Tumours of Haematopoietic and Lymphoid Tissues. IARC; 2017.
Isaacson PG, Chott A. Alpha heavy chain disease: a clinicopathologic study. Am J Surg Pathol. 1993;17(9):897-908.
